coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 9 units (the domain directory itself plus 22.01-22.08), 44 .md files. Matches the expected 9 units / 44 files exactly. Every file was read in full through the 3a (implementer simulation) -> 3b (rubric scoring) -> 3c (devil's advocate) cycle; no sampling. Dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity) and 4 (Constraint Explicitness) are marked N/A for every unit: this domain consumes the ratified four personas from meta/personas.md (D-19) and the project constraint axes from meta/constraints.md, and defines neither. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is scored only on the domain root unit, where named competitors, a capability gap and a moat are genuinely in scope; sub-domain units are not the place that owns competitive positioning, so scoring them would penalise absence of something never in scope. Dimensions 1, 3, 5, 7, 8 are applicable to all 9 units. Applicable checkpoints: 6 (root) + 5 x 8 (sub-domains) = 46. Points 6.5 -> 14.1% raw ambiguity. Roughly ten further candidate findings were generated in 3a and dropped in 3c because they did not survive: broken relative links (22.02.01 line 119 '../22.08-credit-rollup-proof/', 22.08.01 line 126 '../22.06-fraud-anomaly/') change no product behaviour; 22.05-cx line 51 'the choice must be explicit ... rather than defaulted' is resolved by the reference it itself cites (22.05.03 D-01, snapshot is the default); 22.02.02's 'many-to-many' wording versus its fan-out guard is satisfiable as written (pair-key uniqueness plus a separate freeze-for-review guard); 22.02.03's Behavior asserting domain 24's machinery while Q-02 asks which engine is a product-behaviour/component-boundary distinction, not a contradiction; several bare [PENDING] edge-case cells (22.01.04 currency/territory, 22.03.03 curator-removal, 22.06.02 vendor right-of-reply, 22.07.01 non-user/org-watchlist rows) are each covered by a properly owned and targeted open question in the same file; 22.06.02 DT-01's 'the domain's only wont proposal' is a stale-at-writing claim superseded by the later ledger and changes nothing; 22.07 Role Matrix still granting access on 22.07.03 is correct for a documented-but-cut feature.

findings.claim: 22.01.01 and 22.01.03 give different, unmarked numeric thresholds AND different state names for the same freshness classification of the same daily DSP source. 22.01.01 emits healthy < 26h / stale 26h-50h; 22.01.03 -- which 22.01.01 itself names as the owner of the classification -- defines fresh <= 1x cadence and stale 1x-3x cadence with 'DSP daily-batch ~= 24h', i.e. fresh <= 24h / stale 24h-72h. Neither file carries a marker, and 22.01.03's five-state enum has no state called 'healthy'.
findings.evidence: 22.01.01-dsp-account-connection-sync.md:46-52 -- "**Freshness cadence (this feature's emitted expectation).** DSP analytics are daily-batch sources. A connection reports a per-source `last_successful_sync` timestamp; the classification of that timestamp into `healthy` / `stale` / `broken` is 22.01.03's job, but this feature's cadence contract is: a daily source is expected to sync once per 24h, and the concrete thresholds this feature emits are `healthy` when `last_successful_sync < 26h`, `stale` at `26h-50h`, and it flips to `broken` on any auth failure regardless of age." || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:49-50 -- "Cadence = the source's declared expected sync interval (DSP daily-batch = 24h; social varies by platform, declared by the connector). Ages are measured from the last successful sync." || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:54-55 -- "| `fresh` | Last successful sync age <= 1x cadence | Age crosses 1x cadence, or an attempt fails |" and "| `stale` | 1x < age <= 3x cadence, **no** auth failure recorded | A successful sync -> `fresh`; auth failure -> `broken`; age > 3x -> gap opens, stays `stale` until repaired or reclassified |"
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer building the freshness classifier must invent which pair of thresholds is normative (24h/72h or 26h/50h) and whether the enum member is named `fresh` or `healthy`. The thresholds also disagree about what happens between 50h and 72h: under 22.01.01 that range is past `stale` with no successor state defined; under 22.01.03 it is still `stale`. The choice propagates to when a named gap opens (22.01.03 gates gap creation on 'stale past 3x cadence'), and therefore to the Coverage Rule that decides whether 22.08's headline number may be stated at all.

findings.claim: The Coverage Rule -- named by 22.08.01 as 'the sole authority for whether this aggregate may state a number' -- does not place `degraded` sources on either side of its partition. The definition of the attested set A enumerates only `fresh` or `stale`, which excludes `degraded`; the gloss of A's complement enumerates 'missing/broken/terminal/claim-only', which also excludes `degraded`. The two sentences cannot both be satisfied.
findings.evidence: 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:71-76 -- "Let `M` = the set of sources known to have ever contributed to this `(entity, metric)` rollup. Let `A` subset of `M` = sources whose state over the window is `fresh` or `stale` **with no open gap overlapping the window**, contributing an **attested** value (not import-claimed). Let **coverage ratio** `c = |A| / |M|`. Let `dominant-loss` = the largest single-source share of the rollup's total in the last **complete** prior window, among sources currently in `A`'s complement (i.e. missing/broken/terminal/claim-only)." || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:62 -- "`degraded` never opens a gap -- the data is late, not missing." || 22.08.01-contribution-catalog-performance.md:51-54 -- "[22.01.03's **Coverage Rule** ...] is the sole authority for whether this aggregate may state a number. It applies its own source-level dual gate -- source coverage ratio `c` and `dominant-loss` -- independently of record coverage."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a source currently in `degraded` (transient 429/5xx, backoff active) counts toward A. The two readings produce opposite user-visible outcomes on the domain's load-bearing honesty gate: if `degraded` is excluded from A, a rate-limited dominant source pushes dominant-loss >= 0.20 and the rollup refuses to state a figure at all; if it is treated as part of A (which the complement gloss implies, since it lists no `degraded` member), the same rollup states the number plainly. The refusal path also contradicts 22.01.02 D-01's silence-on-transient posture, under which a 429 is deliberately a non-event.

findings.claim: Three files in 22.08 assert that flagged fraudulent streams are excluded once 'at the source' / 'upstream' so that every consumer inherits corrected data, and cite 22.04.01 D-04 as the authority. 22.04.01 D-04 says no such thing: it scopes the exclusion to the geography map. No decision anywhere in the domain establishes a global stream-level fraud filter, so 22.08's non-geographic rollup and its public commercial proof rest on an exclusion that the cited decision does not provide.
findings.evidence: 22.04.01-audience-geography-map.md:98 -- "| D-04 | Flagged fraudulent streams are excluded **in the map**, not at each consumer | Single filter, single truth; duplicated filters drift apart. |" || 22.08-credit-linked-performance-cx.md:84 (R-02) -- "it is a **source-data question already answered upstream**: 22.04.01 D-04 established that flagged streams are excluded once, at the source, and every consumer inherits the correction. Wiring fraud filtering into the proof would put the same filter in a second place, where it can drift. The rule holds here: this sub-domain consumes corrected data and does not re-decide what fraud is." || 22.08.01-contribution-catalog-performance.md:126 -- "Touches **22.06 Fraud / Anomaly** ... the 'fabricated credits' edge case emits a fraud signal; flagged streams are already excluded upstream (cx `R-02`), so this feature consumes corrected data and does not re-decide fraud." || 22.08.03-verified-performance-proof-service-listings.md:58 -- "| Streams later found fraudulent | Excluded upstream (22.04.01 D-04); proof shrinks | Restatement disclosed |" || analytics-market-intelligence-cx.md:22 (CX-05) -- "Flagged streams excluded **at the map**, once -- or bots route real tours to fake demand" and analytics-market-intelligence-cx.md:131 -- "The exclusion happens **once, at the map** (22.04.01 D-04), so every downstream consumer inherits one correction."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent where the fraud filter actually sits. Reading 22.04.01 D-04 literally, the only specified exclusion point is inside the geography map, which is a COULD-tier feature computing per-city audience -- it cannot be the filter for 22.08.01's per-recording stream rollup, and taking it literally leaves 22.08.03 publishing an unfiltered stream total under a 'verified, counter-attested' badge on a public commercial listing. Reading 22.08-cx R-02 instead requires inventing a global ingest-level exclusion that no decision authorises and that 22.05.01 appears to contradict ('Fraudulent streams present | Shown until flagged, corrected after').

findings.claim: The Coverage Rule's tuning constraint is unsatisfiable as written for two of the three constants it names. 'Tunable only upward (stricter), never downward' is coherent for the coverage ratio 0.80, where raising the value is stricter, but for dominant-loss 0.20 and for the 3x-cadence gap trigger raising the value is looser -- so 'upward' and 'stricter' point in opposite directions.
findings.evidence: 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:84-85 -- "Thresholds (`0.80`, `0.20`, the 3x cadence gap trigger) are **defaults**, tunable **only upward** (stricter) by the user, never downward -- an honesty floor a user can lower is not a floor (DT-04)." || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:82 -- "| `c < 0.80` **or** dominant-loss >= 0.20 | **Refuse to state a single figure.** ... A dominant source worth >= 20% of last window's total forces refusal regardless of `c`" (raising 0.20 to 0.30 makes refusal rarer, i.e. looser) || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:60-62 -- "A **named gap** `[start, end]` for `(source, entity, metric)` opens only when the source is `broken`, or `stale` past 3x cadence" (raising 3x to 5x delays the gap, i.e. looser)
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer writing the tuning validator must invent whether the rule is 'the stored value may only increase' (which permits loosening dominant-loss and the gap trigger, defeating D-06's stated purpose) or 'the effective strictness may only increase' (which requires dominant-loss and the gap trigger to be tunable *downward* only, directly against the literal 'never downward'). D-06 restates the same wording without resolving it.

findings.claim: 22.01.02 emits a health state named `actionable` for token expiry, and a UI state 'Needs re-auth'. 22.01.03 owns the freshness state machine and enumerates exactly five states -- fresh, stale, degraded, broken, terminal -- with no `actionable` member; it maps the same user-fixable condition onto `broken`.
findings.evidence: 22.01.02-social-account-connection-sync.md:65 -- "| Access token expires (~60d on Meta, shorter elsewhere) | Ingestion halts at the lapse date; health -> `actionable`; **notifies** (this is the one social failure that is not silent, per D-01) |" || 22.01.02-social-account-connection-sync.md:80 -- "| Needs re-auth | Token expired | Reconnect CTA on the platform card; **notifies** -- the one actionable social failure (D-01)." || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:39-41 -- "**transient vs terminal** -- decides whether the user is told anything at all (22.01.02 D-01). A transient failure (`degraded`) is silent; only user-actionable (`broken`) or permanent (`terminal`) failures surface" || 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:57 -- "| `broken` | An attempt returned auth failure (401/403, `invalid_grant`, `token_revoked`) | User completes re-auth (22.01.01/.02) and next sync succeeds -> `fresh` |"
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether the freshness enum has five members or six, and whether social token expiry is a distinct state or an instance of `broken`. This is the third distinct naming of the same enum across the sub-domain (22.01.01 uses `healthy`, 22.01.03 uses `fresh`, 22.01.02 adds `actionable`), and downstream consumers (22.01.03's Coverage Rule set A, 22.05.02's alert eligibility) branch on state membership.

findings.claim: 22.02.01 makes a per-candidate 'confidence' value load-bearing -- it decides which candidates survive a top-20 cut and it is rendered per candidate -- but never defines how it is computed for any tier except a one-clause hint for `credit-graph`. The sibling feature 22.02.02 uses explicit numeric confidence bands for the same concept, so the two files model confidence differently.
findings.evidence: 22.02.01-external-artist-profile-matching-claiming.md:57-60 -- "the system proposes candidate external profiles derived from their display name, verified credits (domain 02), connected DSP accounts (22.01.01) and social connections (22.01.02). Candidate generation is capped at the top 20 by descending confidence to keep the confirm surface reviewable." || 22.02.01-external-artist-profile-matching-claiming.md:42 -- "Confidence tier: `credit-graph`, scaled by the number of corroborating verified credits." || 22.02.01-external-artist-profile-matching-claiming.md:97 -- "| Populated | Candidates proposed | Candidate list with evidence tier + confidence per candidate |" || 22.02.02-recording-release-catalog-matching.md:61-63 -- "User sees a review list grouped by confidence tier: **auto-matched** (corroborated ISRC/UPC, >= 0.9 confidence), **proposed** (single-signal or fuzzy, 0.5-0.9), **unmatched** (< 0.5, no candidate)."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the confidence scale and the scaling function -- whether confidence is a 0-1 number as in 22.02.02 or an ordinal derived from the four evidence tiers, how 'scaled by the number of corroborating verified credits' maps credits to a value (linear, log, capped), and how confidence is assigned at all for the `dsp-grant`, `first-party` and `self-asserted` tiers. Two implementers produce different top-20 candidate sets and different per-candidate badges from identical inputs.

findings.evidence: 22.04.03-show-impact-attribution.md:46 -- "4. Result: \"Manchester audience up 12-30% over 8 weeks (moderate confidence). A playlist add on 4 March also occurred.\"" || 22.04.03-show-impact-attribution.md:66 -- "| Pending | Show played, window open | \"Measuring -- results in ~6 weeks\" |" || 22.04.03-show-impact-attribution.md:27-29 -- "For each show (from domain 17's booking record), an attribution window opens. findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent both the post-show measurement window and the pre-show baseline window, and must reconcile a result that reports an 8-week movement with a UI that promises it after ~6 weeks. The window length determines when every attribution result appears, which is the one thing the Pending state promises the user.

findings.claim: 22.04.03 treats 'cancelled' and 'rescheduled' as one case and applies the cancelled outcome to both, justifying it with a rationale that is false for a reschedule -- a rescheduled show does happen, just later. Whether a fresh attribution window opens at the new date is unspecified, and the CX file that raises the same case defers it with an ownerless marker to a completed stage.
findings.evidence: 22.04.03-show-impact-attribution.md:55 -- "| Show cancelled/rescheduled after the window opened | Window invalidated, not measured | Nothing measured; a show that didn't happen has no impact. See `#CX-02` synthesis Q5 |" || 22.04.03-show-impact-attribution.md:71 -- "| Invalidated | Show cancelled | Removed silently -- nothing to report |" || 22.04-audience-geography-routing-insight-cx.md:56 -- "5. **State transition conflict**: a cancelled or rescheduled show (common) must invalidate an open attribution window rather than measure a show that never happened. Flagged for Step 5."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a reschedule permanently forfeits attribution for that show (the literal reading of 'Removed silently -- nothing to report') or re-opens a window at the new date. The file calls rescheduling 'common', and 22.04.03 is the sub-domain's loop-closing feature, so the choice decides whether a materially large share of on-platform shows ever produce the measurement the feature exists to produce.

findings.claim: 22.07.02's entire behaviour is threshold-driven -- signals fire when growth crosses a threshold and are suppressed below absolute floors -- but no threshold or floor is quantified anywhere, and unlike every comparable numeric constant in this domain no open question routes them to a calibration stage.
findings.evidence: 22.07.02-momentum-breakout-signals.md:10 -- "Detecting that an artist is accelerating -- growth rates crossing thresholds, engagement deepening, placements compounding -- and telling whoever is watching them." || 22.07.02-momentum-breakout-signals.md:42 -- "| Small artist, small absolute numbers | 3x of nothing is nothing | Floors required; percentage growth on tiny bases is noise |" || 22.07.02-momentum-breakout-signals.md:54 -- "| Fired | Threshold crossed, consent OK, fraud-gated | Signal with the observation and its window |" || 22.07.02-momentum-breakout-signals.md:82 -- "| D-04 | Absolute floors, not just percentage growth | 3x of nothing is nothing, and it would dominate every signal list. |" || contrast 22.07.01-artist-watchlists.md:93 -- "| Q-03 | What cap makes a watchlist a watchlist rather than a scraping tool? A numeric threshold, not a values call. | Agent | `/create-prd-compile` |" and 22.01.03-ingestion-health-gaps-freshness.md:181 -- "| Q-03 | Are the coverage defaults (`0.80`, `0.20`) the right numbers ... | User | `/create-prd-compile` |"
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent which metrics are watched for acceleration, over what comparison window, what multiple constitutes 'crossing', and what absolute floor suppresses a signal. 'Threshold crossed' is untestable as written. The domain has an established pattern of routing exactly this class of constant to /create-prd-compile (22.07.01 Q-03, 22.01.03 Q-03); this feature's three open questions are all values calls and none carries the calibration.
